title: SKYBASE emissions above Genesis Supply are permanently disabled, but Sky Governance keeps a Risk-Framework override Skybase Governance cannot exercise
content:
A.6.1.1.4.2.1.4.2.1.1.6 states that "token emissions beyond the Genesis Supply are permanently disabled; this cannot be reverted by Skybase Governance," and then carves out one exception: "Sky Governance retains the ability to revert where Skybase is in violation of Risk Capital requirements and emissions are required by the Risk Framework."

The interesting content is not the emission cap but the *distribution of authority to modify it*. The party that would benefit from inflating supply — Skybase and its own governance — is the party denied the power. The party allowed to unlock it is the parent ecosystem, and only under a condition that is adverse to Skybase: that Skybase has failed its Risk Capital obligations.

This converts the emission switch from a financing tool into a recapitalization remedy. Dilution becomes something that happens *to* the Agent as a consequence of undercapitalization, never something the Agent can choose for growth or treasury reasons. SKYBASE holders therefore hold a credible supply commitment whose only failure mode is one they can monitor: Risk Capital compliance.

It also shows the general shape of Agent autonomy in the Atlas. Agents get self-governance over their operations, but solvency-relevant levers are reserved to Sky Governance, keeping the Risk Framework enforceable against an Agent that would otherwise be able to opt out of it.
description: Asymmetric authority-to-modify: the Agent cannot unlock its own emissions, while the parent ecosystem can force dilution solely to cure a Risk Capital shortfall.
